_note: THE DECLARED KEYWORD SET.  One axis costs ONE ENTRY HERE, and the
generator emits every .sc entry file and the key->program table from it.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS.  A static-switch axis used to cost nine files: a new
fs_*.sc per fragment family, a JceShaderSet member, a renderer field, a
getter, a destroy, and a selection site per draw path.  The engine has an
axis that WORKS and was measured -- JCE_NO_CSM takes fs_pbr from 8311
instructions to 1549, the 1039 it drops being the PCF taps -- and it was
REVERTED, because the version that wired six of the seven selection sites
silently did nothing on the seventh.  Shape primitives take a path the
wiring had not touched, so forcing the variant on every draw moved ZERO
pixels while the engine's own enable_csm=false moved 7979 on the same
frame.  Half-wired is worse than absent: it is absent AND it looks done.
THE RULE THIS FILE ENFORCES: a program is (vertex variant, fragment
family, keyword bits).  The vertex variant is what the DRAW path is --
static, instanced, skinned -- and it picks its fragment family, because
the varyings have to match.  The keyword bits are what the MATERIAL and
the frame ask for.  Nothing outside the generator writes an entry .sc,
and nothing outside jce_shader_variants.c decides which program a draw
gets.
Regenerate:  python tools/shadergen/gen_shader_variants.py --write
Check only:  python tools/shadergen/gen_shader_variants.py

varying_sets.base: v_texcoord0, v_worldpos, v_normal, v_tangent, v_bitangent, v_viewdepth, v_localpos
varying_sets.tint: v_texcoord0, v_worldpos, v_normal, v_tangent, v_bitangent, v_viewdepth, v_localpos, v_tint

fs_families.name: pbr
fs_families.why: The BASE fragment family: the 16-light brute-force point loop with s_iesLut on stage 14. With no axis set it compiles byte-identically to the historical hand-written fs_pbr.sc, which is the property that let this family be generated without changing a pixel.

fs_families.name: pbr_tint
fs_families.why: Per-instance tint. The body multiplies base albedo by v_tint exactly where a solo draw applies u_baseColorFactor, so an instanced tinted copy is bit-identical to the same mesh drawn solo with that colour while still collapsing into one instanced submit.

fs_families.name: pbr_fade
fs_families.why: LOD cross-fade. vs_pbr_inst_fade smuggles the band-transition coverage in i_data3.w and this screen-door dithers it, so an LOD band change is a fade rather than a pop.

fs_families.name: pbr_inst_tex_array
fs_families.why: Texture-diverse instancing. s_albedo is a SAMPLER2DARRAY and the instance carries its layer, so copies of one mesh that differ by their albedo TEXTURE -- not just a baseColor factor -- batch into one instanced submit.

fs_families.name: pbr_toon
fs_families.why: Cel ramp + rim, per character. Client-facing style, expressed as a fragment family rather than a material branch so a project that never uses it pays nothing.

vertex_variants.name: pbr_skinned
vertex_variants.why: Skinned mesh; the bone palette is the only difference the fragment sees, which is none.

vertex_variants.name: pbr_inst_tint
vertex_variants.why: Instanced copies that differ only by baseColor.

vertex_variants.name: pbr_inst_tex_array
vertex_variants.why: Instanced copies that differ by albedo texture.

axes.name: fwdplus
axes.why: Clustered lighting. Swaps sampler stage 14 from s_iesLut to s_cluster, replaces the 16-light brute-force loop with a per-froxel one, and drops the per-spot IES profile -- a stated tradeoff that keeps WebGL2/GLES3 at 16 fragment samplers. Selected only when the r.forwardplus cvar is on.

axes.name: noshadow
axes.why: Drops the cascade block for a material that does not receive shadows. MEASURED, which is why it is the axis that proves this machinery: fs_pbr is 8311 instructions and CSM is 6766 of them (81.4%), so this is the only axis worth an entry file at all -- a Unity-style pile of material keywords would have been spent on the other 18.6%. No #else is needed: `shadow` is 1.0 above the guarded block and the prologue the rest of the shader consumes stays outside it.
